title: The Spanish flu did not start in Spain.
description:
The Spanish flu did not start in Spain. CBC says the exact origin is difficult to pinpoint, but it did not start in Spain.

Spain's newspapers were free to report it. Spain stayed neutral in the First World War and faced no wartime censorship, says Science Friday. Madrid's ABC reported a strange illness on 22 May 1918.

Fell sick a week after people collapsed in the street, according to Science Friday.

Elsewhere, the news was played down. CBC says officials in other countries chose to suppress the news or downplay how severe the virus was.

Nobody agrees where it began. Science Friday lists China, the American Midwest and France as the suggestions. New America says it is still not agreed.

At least 50 million people died worldwide, according to Science Friday and CBC. New America gives a broad range of 50 million to 100 million.

It was named for the press that reported it, not for where it began.

Sources:
- https://www.sciencefriday.com/articles/the-origin-of-the-spanish-flu/: read (Science Friday, Johanna Mayer, 29 January 2019). Established that Spain stayed neutral and was not subject to wartime censorship, that Madrid's ABC published news of a strange illness on 22 May 1918, that King Alfonso XIII fell sick a week after people collapsed in the street, that experts still disagree on the origin (China, the American Midwest or France), and that at least 50 million people died.
- https://newamerica.org/weekly/down-spanish-flu: read (New America, Rachel Withers, 25 October 2018). Established that Spain's media had no qualms about covering the outbreak, that it first appeared in a headline in Madrid's ABC in May 1918, that the origin is still not agreed, the estimate of 50 million to 100 million deaths, and that fewer than 260,000 took place in Spain.
- https://amp.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.5607552: read (CBC, Under the Influence, Terry O'Reilly). Established that the exact origin is difficult to pinpoint but it did not start in Spain, that Spain was not subject to media censorship, and that officials elsewhere chose to suppress the news or downplay the severity.
